correctness.rationale: The asserted formulas and extremizer families are true. In RESULT.md 32–45, greedy complete-alphabet blocks give a unique half-word decomposition. Each block ends in its previously missing letter; deleting that last letter gives exactly a remainder missing one letter, so S=A/y. Arbitrary incomplete remainders have series R by inclusion-exclusion. For half H with t arches, let m be the sequence of their last letters. The earliest embedding of m and the rightmost embedding of its reverse bound the intervening letters to R R^rev or R c R^rev, where R here denotes the literal remainder. A missing letter gives an absent length-(2t+1) witness if that interior is incomplete; if the center fills its unique missing letter c, the interior has only one c, so m c c m^rev is absent. The separate full-alphabet blocks supply the matching lower bounds, also at t=0. The extremal proof's line 47 overstates the condition on the remainder of an odd host of index at least 2t+1: it applies only with exactly t half-arches. With t+1 or more the odd host already has length at least 2q(t+1)+1, exceeding the claimed optimum. With exactly t the missing-letter condition forces q−1 residual positions and the equality classification follows; the even/odd competing parity bounds are strict as stated. This local proof slip does not invalidate the result. The uploaded verifier was inspected, not run; finite histograms are corroborative only.

evidence: Barker et al. prove the even and odd index rule for each individual palindrome. Adamson counts unrestricted arch blocks and gives unrestricted universal-word enumeration (including Theorem 3.9). The Simon-congruence article treats a related factorization, not this distribution.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The word-level characterization is stronger than a histogram once coupled with complete-arch counts. Unrestricted k-universal totals by themselves are not a palindrome census; the arch enumerator and palindrome proposition together suffice.

evidence: For the known complete-arch series A, all words uniquely consist of a sequence of arches followed by one incomplete remainder, so R=(1−A)/(1−qy). Appending the unique missing letter gives a bijection with a complete arch, so S=A/y. Barker's parity rule then gives the numerator by awarding u rather than 1 to exactly one center for each singly deficient remainder.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Geometric summation of the arch series with weight u² gives the frozen distribution without a new counting identity. The shortest even case needs t minimal q-letter blocks on the half; in the shortest odd case with exactly t arches, the residual half uses q−1 distinct letters and the center is the missing letter. Equality and the q! choices per block/center are direct.

evidence: The mirror's even and odd half-length series are E=R/(1-u²A) and O=[qR+(u−1)S]/(1-u²A), with the same labeled alphabet, remainder conditions and subsequence invariant.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The frozen P is exactly E(z²,u)+zO(z²,u). This is demonstrable duplicate coverage of the distribution, not an inference about either record's priority. The mirror does not explicitly list the shortest-host classification.
